absent: Definitions and numeric values of scaling and timing constants such as ratio scale, fraction base, page size and shift, tick rate, bandwidth interval, ratelimit shift, writeback statistic count, and megabyte to pages conversion.
Behavior of global helpers global_dirty_limits and global_dirtyable_memory and the minimum ratio setter referenced by byte conversion.
Sysfs attribute object definitions linking each show and store handler, including names, permissions, and registration groups beyond table membership.
Workqueue, class registration, debug init, per CPU counter, fraction proportion, and radix tree helper semantics used during init and teardown.
Writeback work handler, dirty throttle control layout, domain selection, position ratio computation, cgroup writeback list management, and block cgroup pin semantics.
Remaining cross dossier symbols beyond the listed stubs and the unlisted remainder of the stub set noted as 29 of 60.
Error code values and tracing hook behavior for bandwidth and ratelimit updates.

findings.text: The public maximum ratio setter bdi_set_max_ratio accepts a percent value, scales it to internal units, and delegates to shared internal validation and update logic.
The companion setter bdi_set_max_ratio_no_scale accepts an already scaled value and forwards it unchanged to the same internal logic, providing a fine grained path.
Internal maximum handling rejects scaled values above one hundred percent and rejects any maximum below the stored minimum, leaving state unchanged and reporting invalid argument on failure.
On acceptance the stored maximum is updated and a proportional fraction share is recomputed from the new maximum relative to one hundred percent.

The minimum and maximum byte getters bdi_get_min_bytes and bdi_get_max_bytes report byte quantities derived from the corresponding stored ratio together with current global dirty thresholds and page size.

The minimum and maximum byte setters translate requested bytes to pages, validate against global dirtyable memory, convert pages to a ratio using current global thresholds, then delegate to ratio setters.
Page validation fails when the request exceeds global dirtyable memory, and page to ratio conversion fails when the global dirty threshold is zero.
The strict limit setter bdi_set_strict_limit accepts only boolean values and toggles BDI_CAP_STRICTLIMIT on the parent object, rejecting other values.

Decimal attribute stores parse user text as unsigned integers or byte counts, forward the parsed value to the matching setter, and report full input length on success while propagating parse or setter failures.
Attribute shows report current minimum and maximum bytes and the boolean strict limit state, while the deprecated stable pages entry always reports zero with a one time removal notice.

The device attribute table aggregates read ahead, coarse and fine minimum and maximum ratio controls, minimum and maximum byte controls, a deprecated stable pages entry, and a strict limit entry, terminated by null.
The bdi device class is registered at init with associated attribute groups, followed by debug infrastructure init, where registration failure aborts init.
Early init creates a system wide writeback workqueue with memory reclaim, unbound, and sysfs visible traits, failing for out of memory when creation fails.

Writeback init wb_init clears the object, links it to its parent, initializes list heads, locks, timestamps, work items, completion tracking, and per CPU statistics, seeding bandwidth and ratelimit fields from INIT_BW.

Shutdown through wb_shutdown is idempotent via the WB_registered marker, where only the first clearer proceeds to unlink from the parent list, drain scheduled work, and require an empty work list, with two build variants differing in unlink locking.
The bdi_lock guard taken in bottom half safe mode protects maximum ratio validation and update including the derived fraction, and also protects strict limit capability updates.
The per writeback list_lock serializes bandwidth timestamp handling, dirtied and written sampling, optional ratelimit refresh, write bandwidth smoothing, and stamp updates.
The per domain lock serializes dirty limit refresh, where callers test the refresh interval without the lock and retest after acquiring it before updating.
The per writeback work_lock taken with interrupts disabled serializes the atomic registered marker clear during shutdown so only one shutdown proceeds.
The cgwb_lock guard taken with interrupts disabled protects parent list removal in one build variant and offline list linkage during release and kill.

Bandwidth refresh from delayed work builds a throttle control for the writeback and invokes shared update logic that optionally refreshes domain limits and ratelimits before smoothing write bandwidth.

Write bandwidth estimation blends recent write progress with prior estimates over a multi second power of two period, applies extra smoothing to suppress spikes, keeps the averaged value above zero, and adjusts the parent total only when dirty IO is present.
Domain dirty limit refresh is paced by a fixed bandwidth interval, jumping immediately up to the current threshold but decaying gradually toward the larger of threshold and current dirty count.
The freerun ceiling is the midpoint of threshold and background threshold, while the hard limit is the larger of threshold and the domain dirty limit.

Dirty ratelimit adaptation compares current dirty level against a midpoint setpoint, derives a task rate from position ratio, estimates a balanced rate from write bandwidth and measured dirty rate capped by write bandwidth, then moves the stored limit by a damped step only when position and rate errors agree, with strict limit mode substituting per writeback dirty and setpoint.

Underflow and division hazards are guarded by clamping elapsed time to at least one tick, flooring written deltas at zero when counters move backward, keeping averaged bandwidth above zero, and rejecting ratio conversion when the dirty threshold is zero.

Cgroup writeback teardown moves from reference release that queues release work on cgwb_release_wq, through shutdown and credential drops under a release mutex, removal from offline tracking, counter teardown, parent reference drop via bdi_put, and deferred memory free via RCU.
Kill handling assumes cgwb_lock is already held, removes radix and membership links, appends the object to the offline list, and terminates its reference count.
The INIT_BW seed corresponds to one hundred megabytes expressed in pages and initializes bandwidth and ratelimit estimates.
The parent release helper bdi_put drops one counted reference and invokes the registered release callback when the count reaches zero.

Per writeback state carries a parent pointer, flush timestamp, four inode lists, list and work locks, work lists and delayed works, bandwidth and ratelimit estimates with stamps and counters, completion tracking, statistics counters, reference and RCU linkage, and cgroup membership nodes.

Parent device info state carries minimum and maximum ratios with a derived proportional fraction, capability flags including strict limit, an aggregate write bandwidth total, a cgroup tree, a release mutex, and a reference count.
Throttle domain state carries a lock, a dirty limit value, and a timestamp controlling when the limit may next be recomputed.
